title: Weak high-order Taylor stationarity with a positive output radius; full space
summary: Find a weak Taylor stationary point of order $m$ in the prescribed domain: output a feasible point and positive radius such that the normalized Taylor decrease in the metric definition is at most $\varepsilon$.

description_paragraphs: The base error is
$$\mathcal{E}(\widehat{x})=\frac{\phi_{f,m}^{\rho}(\widehat{x})}{\chi_m(\rho)}.$$
$$T_{f,m}(x,u)=\sum_{j=0}^m\frac1{j!}D^jf(x)[u^j],\quad\chi_m(\rho)=\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{\rho^j}{j!},$$
$$\phi_{f,m}^{\rho}(x)=f(x)-\min_{x+u\in Q,\ \|u\|_2\le\rho}T_{f,m}(x,u).$$
Here $1\le m\le k$. The radius must be strictly positive, so the denominator is positive. The local constraint set is nonempty and compact, and the Taylor minimum is finite and attained.

output.certificate: The radius is part of the output. No separate trusted certificate is required, but all Taylor-model inequalities in the definition must hold.
description_paragraphs: Return $(\widehat{x},\rho)$ with $\widehat{x}\in Q$ and $0<\rho\le1$; the radius is part of the output.
The output may be an unqueried point, a feasible average of past iterates, or another feasible postprocessing result. No function value or additional computable certificate is required.

Fix $k\ge2$ and $0<\nu\le1$.
The feasible domain in this specification is $Q=\mathbb{R}^d$.

proofs.title: Weak Taylor stationarity with a freely chosen positive radius
proofs.statement: In the unconstrained free-radius specification, an approximate first-order stationary point suffices for weak high-order Taylor stationarity.
proofs.body:
Define $\phi_{f,m}^{\rho}(x)=f(x)-\min_{\|s\|\le\rho}T_{f,m}(x,s)$ and $\chi_m(\rho)=\sum_{j=1}^m\rho^j/j!$. First obtain $\|\nabla f(x)\|\le\varepsilon/2$. Using one complete jet at x if necessary, select a finite $0<\rho\le1$ so small that
$$\sum_{j=2}^m\frac{\|D^jf(x)\|}{j!}\rho^{j-1}\le\varepsilon/2.$$
All coefficients are finite and known, so this selection uses only internal computation. The Taylor decrease over the $\rho$-ball is at most $\varepsilon\rho$, and $\rho\le\chi_m(\rho)$. Hence $\phi_{f,m}^{\rho}(x)\le\varepsilon\chi_m(\rho)$.

This proves sufficiency, not a converse from weak Taylor stationarity to a small gradient. Consequently, sharpness of a particular regularization method with prescribed step or radius rules is not automatically a minimax lower bound for arbitrary algorithms free to choose $\rho$. The method-specific lower result in CGTweak, Theorem 5.4, retains that restricted scope. For a constrained feasible set, use feasible Taylor decrease; the Euclidean gradient criterion cannot silently replace constrained stationarity.
proofs.scope: Unconstrained weak Taylor criterion with an algorithm-selected positive radius. Does not apply directly to strong orderwise Taylor tolerances or arbitrary constrained geometry.
proofs.limitations: The mapped bound retains its complete model, oracle, algorithm view, guarantee, quantity, resource projection, and parameter-region conditions. This argument does not enlarge that scope.
